deductions: "each live cell is exactly one of {0, 1, 4}" / "a one-hot cell encoding" (channels overlap; there is no empty channel, and ch0 is the agent)
"Channel 2 ... Never active anywhere" (ch2 is the always-on goal row, row 1, columns 1-8)
"Channel 3 is always on outside the live area ... the top margin is two rows thick" (row 1 is the goal row, ch2; the true border is 36 cells in ch3)
marks.conclusion: A small tanh/ELU 500-32-32-5 MLP on a one-hot 10x10x5 grid with a wall border; either a policy over 5 actions or a 5-way classifier; maybe a lane-crossing game, but unsettled.
marks.judge_notes: Rulings: Activation 1 of 2: it argues from the weights (a dead unit pinned at a constant -1 would make W2 row ~ -b2) and rules out ReLU and sigmoid, and the answer 'tanh or ELU' contains the right one, but it does not tell tanh from ELU; I gave half. Another judge could give 0 or 2. Channel meanings 1 (ch3 wall/padding only); ch0 'decision-relevant', ch1/ch4 'object or terrain' are too vague. Layout 2: border, ch1 rows 2-7 only in 4-column lanes, ch0/ch4 rows 2-8, centre weights; the goal row is misplaced in the border. Name 0: 'looks a lot like a lane-crossing grid game' is raised as a hypothesis and the final summary says the exact game cannot be determined, so I did not count it as committing. Depth level 1: gating observations (L2 units 7 and 24 as switches for outputs 3 and 4) cannot be confirmed against the fact sheet. B_actions 0: '5 actions (e.g. stay plus four moves) or a 5-way classifier' is not committed. Training: no RL claim, 0.
